{"findings": [
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 50, "severity": "high", "category": "concurrency", "title": "Async legacy writes derived from the request context may be cancelled", "body": "In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the fire-and-forget goroutine calls `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming HTTP request context. That context is cancelled as soon as the API handler returns, which happens immediately after the unified-storage write succeeds. The legacy write can therefore be aborted with 'context canceled' before it even starts, so legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage. The legacy call should use a detached/background context (with only the logger carried over), not the request context."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 134, "severity": "high", "category": "concurrency", "title": "Update goroutine shares objInfo with the request, causing races and non-idempotent updates", "body": "The previous implementation wrapped objInfo with `updateWrapper` to force both stores to write the same computed object. Now `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` is invoked asynchronously with the same `objInfo` that unified storage already consumed. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` implementations are not required to be thread-safe or idempotent (they can run arbitrary mutate funcs, and often the returned object is mutated in place by storage layers). The legacy goroutine re-invokes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` concurrently with the caller continuing to use the result, which is a data race and can produce a different object in legacy than in unified storage, breaking the dual-write guarantee."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 45, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "Create failure records the wrong metric (legacy instead of storage)", "body": "When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. This counts unified-storage failures/errors against the legacy-storage metric, corrupting the dualwriter duration/error metrics used to monitor migration health. It should call `recordStorageDuration`."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 129, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "Update failure records the wrong metric (legacy instead of storage)", "body": "When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, attributing the storage error and its latency to the legacy-storage metric. Same class of mislabeling as the Create path; should be `recordStorageDuration`."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 166, "severity": "medium", "category": "bug", "title": "DeleteCollection goroutine records legacy write under the storage metric", "body": "In the DeleteCollection goroutine, the legacy call duration is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)`. The async legacy delete-collection latency and error status are therefore reported as unified-storage metrics, making both series wrong. It should call `recordLegacyDuration`."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 106, "severity": "low", "category": "bug", "title": "Delete success passes `name` where the `kind` label is expected", "body": "On successful unified-storage delete, the metric is recorded as `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` — every other call passes `options.Kind` as that argument. The `kind` metric label will instead contain the object name, producing unbounded label cardinality and inconsistent data for the delete method."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 97, "severity": "low", "category": "bug", "title": "Delete builds a context with the wrong logger, dropping name/kind/method fields", "body": "In Delete, after building `log := d.Log.WithValues(\"name\", name, \"kind\", options.Kind, \"method\", method)`, the code does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` (the bare logger) instead of `log`. The contexted logger used downstream loses the name/kind/method attributes, so error logs from Delete lack the identifying fields present in all other methods."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go", "line": 55, "severity": "medium", "category": "data", "title": "Async legacy write failures are only counted in metrics, never logged or retried", "body": "In all four write paths the result of the asynchronous legacy write (`errObjectSt` / `err`) is passed only to `recordLegacyDuration` and discarded; there is no `log.Error` and no retry/queue mechanism. The PR description calls the legacy write 'a safe measure', but a silent failure leaves the two stores permanently divergent with only a Prometheus counter as evidence. At minimum the error should be logged (as the previous implementation did with log.Error), otherwise operators have no way to discover divergence."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go", "line": 63, "severity": "medium", "category": "test_gap", "title": "Tests never assert that the async legacy write actually happens", "body": "Mode 3 now writes to legacy storage in an un-awaited goroutine. The new tests (e.g. TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Update, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_DeleteCollection) set up legacy mock expectations but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or otherwise wait for/sync the goroutine, and `wantErr` cases return before the goroutine's mock call is checked. So the tests can pass even if the legacy write never executes or executes after the test finishes, and the error-path cases (e.g. 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' only sets up a legacy mock that should not be called) actually verify the wrong store. Use mock.AssertExpectations with a channel/waitgroup or testify's assert.Eventually to make the async behavior deterministic."},
  {"file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go", "line": 119, "severity": "low", "category": "bug", "title": "TestMode3_Get shadows the shared prometheus registry with a local one", "body": "TestMode3_Get declares `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` inside the subtest, shadowing the package-level `p` used by all other tests in the file. This looks like an accidental leftover from moving the registry to package scope (the corresponding line was removed from dualwriter_mode1_test.go in this same PR). While harmless functionally, it makes the test inconsistent with the rest of the file and can hide future refactoring mistakes; the local declaration should be removed."}
]}

findings.title: Async legacy writes derived from the request context may be cancelled
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the fire-and-forget goroutine calls `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` where `ctx` is the incoming HTTP request context. That context is cancelled as soon as the API handler returns, which happens immediately after the unified-storage write succeeds. The legacy write can therefore be aborted with 'context canceled' before it even starts, so legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage. The legacy call should use a detached/background context (with only the logger carried over), not the request context.

findings.title: Update goroutine shares objInfo with the request, causing races and non-idempotent updates
findings.body: The previous implementation wrapped objInfo with `updateWrapper` to force both stores to write the same computed object. Now `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` is invoked asynchronously with the same `objInfo` that unified storage already consumed. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` implementations are not required to be thread-safe or idempotent (they can run arbitrary mutate funcs, and often the returned object is mutated in place by storage layers). The legacy goroutine re-invokes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` concurrently with the caller continuing to use the result, which is a data race and can produce a different object in legacy than in unified storage, breaking the dual-write guarantee.

findings.title: Create failure records the wrong metric (legacy instead of storage)
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with the storage start time. This counts unified-storage failures/errors against the legacy-storage metric, corrupting the dualwriter duration/error metrics used to monitor migration health. It should call `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Update failure records the wrong metric (legacy instead of storage)
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`, attributing the storage error and its latency to the legacy-storage metric. Same class of mislabeling as the Create path; should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: DeleteCollection goroutine records legacy write under the storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine, the legacy call duration is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)`. The async legacy delete-collection latency and error status are therefore reported as unified-storage metrics, making both series wrong. It should call `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Delete success passes `name` where the `kind` label is expected
findings.body: On successful unified-storage delete, the metric is recorded as `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` — every other call passes `options.Kind` as that argument. The `kind` metric label will instead contain the object name, producing unbounded label cardinality and inconsistent data for the delete method.

findings.title: Delete builds a context with the wrong logger, dropping name/kind/method fields
findings.body: In Delete, after building `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, the code does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` (the bare logger) instead of `log`. The contexted logger used downstream loses the name/kind/method attributes, so error logs from Delete lack the identifying fields present in all other methods.

findings.title: Async legacy write failures are only counted in metrics, never logged or retried
findings.body: In all four write paths the result of the asynchronous legacy write (`errObjectSt` / `err`) is passed only to `recordLegacyDuration` and discarded; there is no `log.Error` and no retry/queue mechanism. The PR description calls the legacy write 'a safe measure', but a silent failure leaves the two stores permanently divergent with only a Prometheus counter as evidence. At minimum the error should be logged (as the previous implementation did with log.Error), otherwise operators have no way to discover divergence.

findings.title: Tests never assert that the async legacy write actually happens
findings.body: Mode 3 now writes to legacy storage in an un-awaited goroutine. The new tests (e.g. TestMode3_Create, TestMode3_Update, TestMode3_Delete, TestMode3_DeleteCollection) set up legacy mock expectations but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` or otherwise wait for/sync the goroutine, and `wantErr` cases return before the goroutine's mock call is checked. So the tests can pass even if the legacy write never executes or executes after the test finishes, and the error-path cases (e.g. 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' only sets up a legacy mock that should not be called) actually verify the wrong store. Use mock.AssertExpectations with a channel/waitgroup or testify's assert.Eventually to make the async behavior deterministic.

findings.title: TestMode3_Get shadows the shared prometheus registry with a local one
findings.body: TestMode3_Get declares `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` inside the subtest, shadowing the package-level `p` used by all other tests in the file. This looks like an accidental leftover from moving the registry to package scope (the corresponding line was removed from dualwriter_mode1_test.go in this same PR). While harmless functionally, it makes the test inconsistent with the rest of the file and can hide future refactoring mistakes; the local declaration should be removed.
